 Jayson Tatum finished Sunday’s win over the Magic with 32 points (8-of-19 FGs, 15-of-17 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and one three-pointer.
 Tatum didn’t have his best day shooting the basketball, but his ability to get to the foul line paid off immensely. He made 15 of his 17 free-throw attempts, the second time in three games that the Celtics’ forward has scored at least 15 points on free throws. Add in the assists and blocks, and this was a solid end to the week for those rostering Tatum. Boston plays four games next week, starting with the Rockets on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jayson Tatum amassed 26 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Tatum has scored 23 points or more in each of his last four games, rebounding well after a quiet outing in Boston’s season opener. Against the Bulls, he scored 16 of his 26 points in the first half, shooting 7-of-11 from the field. Tatum cooled off after halftime, but it didn’t matter much as Boston had already built up a large lead. He’ll look to finish the week on a high when the Celtics face the Magic on Sunday.

 Jayson Tatum accounted for 40 points (10-of-20 FGs, 18-of-22 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nets. 
 The Celtics’ second game in as many nights was more dramatic than many expected, as they needed overtime and a Tatum pull-up at the buzzer to beat the Nets. He finished with an excellent stat line, shooting 50 percent from the field and committing no turnovers. Counting the postseason, this was Tatum’s first 40-point game since Game 4 of the Celtics’ 2025 second-round series against the Knicks (the game in which he was injured).

 Jayson Tatum lit up the Bulls with 23 points (7-of-17 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers on Monday. 
 After dropping 36 points on Friday, Tatum’s scoring dipped a bit in this game. It was a slightly subpar shooting night, but he also didn’t need to score as much. Boston led by 30 points at the end of the third quarter, and the lineup that dominated the third quarter didn’t include Tatum, so he only played 28 minutes. They’ll take on the Nets on Tuesday, which will be the second night of this back-to-back. Tatum should be in for a better outing.

 Jayson Tatum amassed 36 points (14-of-26 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Knicks. 
 After recording an inefficient double-double in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons, Tatum was outstanding in Friday’s home opener. He hit multiple shots down the stretch to hold off the Knicks, and the Celtics star committed just two turnovers. Tatum also got to the foul line Friday, something he didn’t do against the Pistons. As the unquestioned top scoring option, Tatum will need to make use of the foul line consistently, as it would benefit him and the Celtics as a whole. Boston plays four games in Week 2, starting with a Monday/Tuesday back-to-back against the Bulls and Nets.

 Jayson Tatum recorded a double-double on Tuesday with 13 points (6-of-23 FGs), four rebounds and 11 assists against the Pistons. 
 Tatum had a decent first half and entered the break with 11 points. Unfortunately, he wasn’t able to replicate any of that success after halftime. He shot 1-of-10 from the floor in the second half, which wasn’t enough for Boston to hold onto the big lead they took in the third quarter. It was a rough start to the year for him, though he was the primary playmaker for them. If he can continue to dish out the dimes like he did in this game, he could be in for a strong season, especially once the shooting percentage evens out.

 Jayson Tatum finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Hornets with 19 points (8-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, six assists, two steals and three three-pointers. 
 The Celtics have one more preseason game, Friday night in Philadelphia, and Tatum’s Wednesday workload could mean he sits that one out. He played 29 minutes against Charlotte and led all scorers with 19 points. Tatum also recorded six assists, and Payton Pritchard was the only Celtic with more. Tatum has a first-round ADP in Yahoo drafts, and with good reason. As long as he stays healthy, JT should be an elite fantasy option in any league format.

 Jayson Tatum amassed 23 points (9-of-19 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 26 minutes, leading the Celtics to a 144-106 blowout win over the 76ers in preseason action on Saturday. 
 The Celtics looked early on like a team with a lot of guys playing together for the first time before Tatum started to assert himself from a facilitating and scoring standpoint. Things turned around rather quickly afterwards as the new-look Tatum and Paul George combination seemed like a natural fit playing together on both ends of the floor. He also made sure to involve offseason acquisition Mitchell Robinson with a couple early pick-and-roll opportunities. It’s abundantly clear that this version of the Celtics has been built to revolve entirely around Tatum with an assortment of quality complementary pieces. The 28-year-old franchise cornerstone looks completely healthy after missing most of last year recovering from an Achilles injury and will be a top-five range pick in most fantasy drafts this fall.

 Jayson Tatum (knee) said on Monday that he “feels great” going into Celtics training camp. 
 After suffering a ruptured Achilles tendon in the second round of the 2025 playoffs, Tatum surprised many by returning to action in early March. However, the Celtics star played only 16 games before a lingering left knee issue kept him out of Game 7 of Boston’s first-round series against Philadelphia. The good news is that Tatum spent most of his offseason getting “stronger and more explosive” instead of rehab, and he “feels great” going into training camp. That’s excellent news for the Celtics and for fantasy managers, who should look to select Tatum in the first round of standard league drafts.

 Jayson Tatum (knee) is out for Saturday’s Game 7 against the 76ers. 
 Tatum’s left leg gave him trouble during Boston’s Game 6 loss to the 76ers, but Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla was confident on Friday that the star forward would be available for Game 7. Added to the injury report early Saturday afternoon, Tatum is now officially out. Jordan Walsh and Baylor Scheierman are potential replacements in the starting lineup, with the former being the more likely choice due to what he brings to the table defensively.

 Jayson Tatum (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s Game 7 against the 76ers. 
 Tatum was added to the injury report Saturday afternoon as questionable with left knee stiffness. It’s not a good sign for the 28-year-old power forward. Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla told reporters on Friday that Tatum would play. Now his superstar’s status is legitimately up in the air on the afternoon of Game 7.

 Nembhard has scored at least 18 points in each of his last three games, all played without Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring).  Jay Huff missed both of his shot attempts in Sunday’s loss to the Nets, finishing with zero points and three rebounds.
 It’s fair to say that Huff’s four starts for the injured Ivica Zubac (ankle) have not gone as well as many fantasy managers hoped. While he scored 13 points in Friday’s loss to the Heat, he has totaled 22 points, 16 rebounds and one block in those four games. Huff appeared to tweak his right foot in the first half of Sunday’s defeat but returned. Managers still holding onto him in hopes of getting some streaming value may be best served by moving on to another option going into Week 3.

 Pascal Siakam tallied 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in Sunday’s loss to the Nets.
 In the three games the Pacers have played since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam has averaged 18.7 points per game while shooting 45.8 percent from the field. That isn’t necessarily bad, but not sharing the floor with a lead guard as talented as Haliburton lowers Siakam’s ceiling. On Sunday, he scored just four points in the second half, shooting 1-of-3 from the field. The Pacers play three games next week, starting with the Hawks on Monday.

 Nolan Traoré accounted for 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
 Having started the Nets’ last three games, Traoré’s production has been inconsistent. He rebounded nicely from a poor outing against the Pistons on Friday, scoring in double figures for the third time in four games. Traoré shot 4-of-8 from beyond the arc and committed one turnover in 30 minutes. Monday’s matchup against the Knicks will be more challenging, and Mikel Brown Jr. (back) should be available, which may limit Traoré’s ceiling.

 Day’Ron Sharpe amassed 15 points (5-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
 Playing against a Pacers team without Ivica Zubac or Obi Toppin, Sharpe had his most productive game of the season. The Nets center recorded his first double-double in six games, finishing with new highs in points and rebounds. Sharpe didn’t record any defensive stats, ending his two-game streak with at least one steal and one block. He’ll look to do more on that end of the floor on Monday when the Nets visit the Knicks.

 Despite shooting 1-of-6 from inside the arc, Randle finished Sunday’s victory with his third 20-point game of the season. That said, his performance against the Pacers was better than Friday’s showing against the Pistons.

 The Nets got their first win of the season on Sunday, and getting Porter involved early helped. The Nets forward scored seven points in the first quarter and 13 in the first half. After attempting nine shots in Friday’s loss to the Pistons, Porter nearly matched that number in the first quarter (seven).
